1.bug_analyze:
When you have an SQL string literal that contains escaped single quotes (''hello world'') and then on a following line you start a comment with “--”, the highlighter must close out the string literal correctly before entering comment mode. In the buggy rendering the entire comment line (and the second VALUES clause) was still being treated as part of the preceding string, so the comment markers weren’t recognized and the comment text was colored like a string.
The correct rendering should show:
- The first INSERT and its VALUES string all highlighted properly (keywords in blue, strings in yellow/green).
- Then on the next line “-- this is a comment” rendered in the comment color (gray), not in string color.
- Finally the second INSERT/VALUES clause rendered again with its own string literal colors, not as part of the comment or first string.
1.patch_analyze: In the patched image the comment line is now shown in the proper comment color (gray), and the string literal from the first VALUES has been correctly terminated before the comment. The second INSERT/VALUES clause also returns to normal keyword/string coloring. That matches the expected behavior.
